items.title: Delhi High Court asks Amitabh Bachchan to appear personally if he wants to continue personality rights case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday said veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan will have to appear personally before the Court if he wishes to pursue his personality rights suit [Amitabh Bachchan v Rajat Nagi & Ors] . Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said that if the Bachchan is unable to settle the matter between one or more defendants, and he then wants to pursue the case in court, he will have to be present in Court. The Court passed the direction on October 9 while granting Bachchan time to complete the formalities of an amicable settlement reached with some of the defendants. The Court was informed that although a settlement had been arrived at with some of the defendants, it could not be formally signed due to logistical issues on the actor’s part. “In the event of non-settlement or incomplete settlement, if the plaintiff wishes to pursue the suit on any of the claims or issues, the plaintiff shall remain personally present on the next date of hearing, enabling the Court to exercise its powers under Order X Rule 2 read with Order V Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023,” the Court ordered. items.title: A walk to forget? Why Delhi High Court slapped ₹10,000 costs on advocate
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday imposed costs of ₹10,000 on an advocate for appearing in court virtually while walking in the garden. Justice Om Prakash Shukla said that the lawyer's conduct was in violation of the Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025. "Learned Counsel is appearing in this matter while walking in the garden and the connection is also not proper. This is in violation of the Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025 of this Court. Accordingly, costs of Rs.10,000/- is imposed on the learned counsel for the petitioner, to be deposited before the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee within a week from today," the Court ordered. It added that on the next date of hearing on November 4, the counsel must appear in person. The Court passed the order while dealing with an arbitration petition. Notably, this is not the first time Justice Shukla has objected to persons appearing virtually in improper manner. Last month, he had fined a lawyer ₹1 lakh for appearing in court while sitting in a moving car. He observed that the convenience of virtual proceedings cannot come at the cost of courtroom decorum or disrupt the conduct of judicial proceed
